title: A Clock for the Uniform
premise: In the winter of 1917, Marguerite Blackwood works her late father's typeface bench in a small French print shop, cutting punches for the town's only press. When occupying soldiers requisition the shop and seize the civic ledger bearing every resident's name, she is forced to keep printing under their command while secretly recutting the ledger's type to hide neighbors marked for conscription. Torn between a wounded officer who questions his orders and her duty to the townspeople who once shunned her family, she races to finish the forged pages before the armistice — knowing either outcome could save or condemn them. In the end, the armistice arrives hours after she burns the original plates; the town survives, the officer chooses exile over duty, and Marguerite finally signs her own name in ink.
about_author: Noor Eastwick is the pen name of a former letterpress apprentice who spent a decade restoring nineteenth-century type cabinets in provincial French workshops. Their fiction explores quiet acts of resistance rendered in ink, metal, and paper.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Letters
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She cuts a new punch by lamplight while the town whispers of approaching armies; flashbacks establish her father's death and the townsfolk's cold tolerance of the Blackwood name. Emotional beat: lonely competence — she belongs to her work because nowhere else will have her.

chapters.title: Requisition at First Light
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Soldiers occupy the square; Captain Aurel Vasseur seizes the civic ledger and orders the shop converted to army printing. He notices her steady hands and drafts her on the spot. Emotional beat: fear sharpened into defiance as her invisibility ends with a signature she never chose to give.

chapters.title: Names in Cold Type
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Reading the ledger at night, she finds neighbors' names flagged for conscription lists — including the baker's son who once mocked her father. Emotional beat: the discovery that survival and complicity are printed on the same page, and she holds the type.

chapters.title: The Officer Who Reads
chapters.summary: Vasseur's POV. He watches Marguerite work, recognizing craft that outstrips her station, and confides a letter home he cannot send. Emotional beat: reluctant respect curdling into guilt — he begins to see the names as people, not requisitions.

chapters.title: A Punch Cut Twice
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She begins secretly recutting flagged names into unremarkable variants, working nights after army proofs are done. The baker's widow nearly catches her. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into purpose; for the first time, the town needs her.

chapters.title: Inspection
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. A colonel arrives to audit the ledger against fresh rolls; Vasseur must choose whether to report the discrepancies he half-suspects. Emotional beat: love against duty made literal — each protects the other by lying badly, and both know it.

chapters.title: What the Widow Knew
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The baker's widow reveals she has known for weeks and offers the resistance's escape route — but taking it means abandoning the unfinished pages. Emotional beat: belonging offered at last, priced exactly at the work she cannot leave.

chapters.title: Armistice Rumors
chapters.summary: Vasseur's POV. Peace talks stall; orders come down to finalize all conscription lists within days. He warns Marguerite obliquely through a proof correction. Emotional beat: the clock becomes real — every hour of cutting now measured against a deadline neither controls.

chapters.title: The Last Impression
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, climax. On the final night she prints the altered ledger, destroys the original plates in the foundry furnace as soldiers pound the door, and Vasseur falsifies the inspection report to cover her. Emotional beat: sacrifice at full heat — he burns his career, she burns her father's legacy, and the pages survive.

chapters.title: Signed in Ink
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, resolution. Armistice comes at dawn; the town counts its sons and finds them all present. Vasseur departs for voluntary exile, leaving her his unsent letter. She sets her own name in type and pulls one clean proof. Emotional beat: quiet triumph — belonging no longer given, but made, letter by letter.
